question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{2}(t)-4,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{2}{s-2}-\frac{1}{s-4}+\frac{1}{s},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{1}{s-4}+\frac{1}{s}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{2}{s-2}-\frac{1}{s-4}+\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & =2\,{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}\}-{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\}+{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & =2{e}^{2\cdot t}-{e}^{4\cdot t}+1 \\  & =-{e}^{4t}+2{e}^{2t}+1 \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}+\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\}+{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\} \\  & ={e}^{4\cdot t}+1 \\  & ={e}^{4t}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{4t}+2{e}^{2t}+1 \\ {e}^{4t}+1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
